item.title: CORPORATE GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS INTERN
item.description:
HII is America's largest shipbuilder and a global, all-domain defense provider with a 140-year history of advancing U.S. national defense. This is a 2027 Government Affairs summer internship (minimum 10 weeks) at HII's corporate office in Arlington, Virginia. The intern supports the Government and Customer Relations (GCR) team, whose work is connected to HII's Washington, DC office, and gains exposure to business, finance, information technology, legal and government affairs while supporting the leaders driving HII's future.
Key responsibilities: Support the GCR team through assignments related to policy analysis, legislative affairs and political affairs. Conduct research on legislative bills and activity related to defense issues. Attend congressional hearings and think tank events focused on national security and write summary reports. Assist with Political Action Committee (PAC) recruitment and operational projects. Create key presentations and manage assignments that support GCR's mission and annual deliverables.
Qualifications: Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher (official transcripts required). Enrolled in a relevant degree program, typically business, management, accounting, economics/finance, tax accounting, computer information science or information technology, communications, marketing, English, or human resources. Currently attending a 4-year college or university (or 2+2 program), ideally a rising junior or above who returns to school in the fall after the internship, or currently enrolled in a relevant master's program. Ability to work a 40-hour week for a minimum of 10 weeks during the summer. U.S. citizenship is required, and a valid email address is required to apply. Preferred: previous Hill, political or government office experience. Salary range: $44,988 to $69,412, with final pay depending on experience and qualifications.
Application requirements: Applicants must provide their school name, degree program and major, anticipated graduation date, current academic level, and overall GPA on a 4.0 scale, and must upload a copy of unofficial transcripts. Applications missing requested information may be disqualified.
Logistics: The application deadline is Sunday, November 1, 2026. The role is 40 hours per week on site. Telework and relocation assistance are not available, though housing assistance may be available.

item.title: Research Intern (Summer 2027)
item.description:
CNA is hiring a Research Intern for Summer 2027 at its Arlington, Virginia location. Interns are embedded in real study teams and either take on a self-contained research project or support multiple ongoing studies, applying rigorous analysis to real-world defense and security challenges. The role offers hands-on experience, mentorship, and networking opportunities in a collaborative, mission-driven environment.
Key responsibilities: Assist in defining and structuring analytical problems. Develop sound analytical techniques. Carry out analyses to logical conclusions. Communicate results both in writing and orally. Collaborate with expert researchers and analysts on complex national security issues. Contribute to projects that inform defense policy and operations. Present findings and insights to internal teams and potentially external stakeholders. Perform other duties as assigned.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in the physical sciences, engineering, operations research, mathematics, statistics, economics, international relations, or a related discipline. Applicants must be enrolled in a graduate program (master's or PhD) and have a strong interest in policy research, national defense, or security studies. Undergraduate research experience, including literature searches, analyses, and report writing, is required, and graduate-level coursework and experience are preferred. Required skills include experience with database manipulation and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), good interpersonal and oral and written communication, critical thinking, and organizational skills. Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance, and U.S. citizenship is required.
Application and logistics: Apply by November 30, 2026. Preference is given to candidates who upload a resume, a cover letter describing their experience and why they want to intern with CNA, and transcripts (unofficial copies are accepted). The position is eligible for telecommuting or hybrid work at the supervisor's discretion, and interns may be required to work at CNA headquarters or other locations. All applicants are subject to a background investigation.

item.title: Internship
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/09/2026.
PIRG is a consumer advocacy organization working on solutions to problems that affect health, safety and well-being. It is hiring interns to work with its issue advocacy teams and its state offices across the country; the posting lists the department as Program and State and the workplace type as hybrid. Interns learn the basics of organizing and put those skills to work on public interest issues including consumer protection, public health, transportation, plastic pollution and more.
What interns do: Help educate and engage people on PIRG's issues, whether by getting issues into the media, helping grow coalitions, or organizing events, to build the public support needed to win. Learn how to analyze problems, push for smart solutions, and build public support for PIRG's goals. Work side-by-side with a staff member, learning the ropes. Attend briefings and trainings to learn more about the issues and gain organizing skills.
Who should apply: People who care deeply about solving these issues and are ready to make a difference now. The posting describes the internship as one of the best ways to gain experience for a career in political advocacy. No specific degree or experience requirements are listed.
Logistics: Interns are hired nationwide for fall, spring and summer terms. Applicants should indicate on the application which office or offices, and which term, they are applying for. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Internships are unpaid. PIRG is an equal opportunity employer.

item.title: Summer Research Assistant, Responsible Investing - Y Analytics
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/09/2026.
TPG is a leading global alternative asset management firm, founded in San Francisco in 1992, investing across private equity, impact, credit, real estate and market solutions. Y Analytics is TPG's internal capability for understanding and improving the environmental and social impacts of deployed capital. It supports impact assessment for The Rise Fund, the TPG Rise Climate Fund and other TPG vehicles, as well as responsible investing and sustainability across TPG and its portfolio. The Responsible Investing Research Assistant supports academic and industry research and analysis of the social impact of existing and potential investments, prepares thought leadership, and helps drive improved performance on responsible investing and sustainability factors across TPG's global portfolio.
Key responsibilities: Contribute to fast-paced teams conducting research, deal work and engagement with portfolio companies on responsible investing topics, including human capital management, external stakeholder relations, environmental health and safety, climate and other sustainability topics. Conduct and synthesize market research. Support academic and industry research on social impact. Prepare thought leadership.
Qualifications: Authorization to work in the U.S. (employment-based immigration sponsorship is not available). Undergraduate student who has completed at least two years of study, or a graduate student, pursuing a degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Sustainability, Business, Economics, Public Administration or another relevant program. Experience or demonstrated interest in responsible investing, corporate social responsibility, climate/sustainability, consulting, finance, impact investing or a related field. Ability to use AI-enabled research and productivity tools effectively, responsibly and with appropriate judgement. Excellent Excel and PowerPoint skills. Excellent written and spoken communication skills and fluency in English. Experience with sustainability performance assessment or reporting frameworks (e.g., SASB, GRI) is a plus.
Compensation and logistics: $22.50 per hour, 40 hours per week, early June to late August 2027. The role is remote, and interns must be located during the internship in one of the following: AZ, CA, DC, FL, GA, IL, NJ, NY, TN, TX, VA, WI, AR, CO, IN, KY, LA, MA, MI, MN, MO, NE, NH, NC, OH, PA, SC, UT, WA, WY. In-person work may be an option for those near a TPG office.
How to apply: Instead of a cover letter, submit a written response of no more than one page (excluding citations) to the prompt in the posting. Choose a responsible investing theme, explain why it matters to investors or companies, synthesize one or two findings or debates, identify risks, opportunities or implementation considerations, and pose one question that deserves further research. Use standard document formatting and cite sources. Only applications submitted through the TPG careers page (https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/tpgcareers) will be considered.

item.company: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
item.title: 2026 CDC Public Health Fellowships
item.description:
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) supports education, training and development across the public health workforce, including postgraduate experiential service-learning fellowships. Its Public Health Fellowships prepare fellows to protect the nation's health, filling workforce gaps in epidemiology, policy, economic analysis, data science, laboratory science, public health service delivery and more. Three fellowships are currently accepting applications, and most are based in Atlanta, GA. This listing was published by ProFellow on behalf of CDC.
The fellowships: (1) Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program: paid 2-year applied training for doctoral- or master's-prepared professionals, applying computer science, data analytics and data science to public health needs. (2) Steven M. Teutsch Prevention Effectiveness (PE) Fellowship: a paid 2-year postdoctoral research fellowship in quantitative policy analysis, health economics-based inquiry and integrative health services research, assessing the effectiveness, quality and cost of public health policies, programs and practices. (3) Evaluation Fellowship Program: a paid 2-year fellowship for master's and doctoral recipients in which fellows build evaluation skills while helping their host program build, expand or improve its evaluation activities.
Qualifications: These are postgraduate programs. Informatics requires a doctoral or master's degree, the Prevention Effectiveness Fellowship is postdoctoral, and the Evaluation Fellowship is for master's and doctoral recipients. Each fellowship has its own detailed eligibility requirements, which are on CDC's fellowships webpage and not in this listing.
Compensation and benefits: Salary depends on the fellow's degree (master's or doctorate), with a posted range of $84,238 to $100,964. Benefits include health, vision and dental coverage, retirement benefits, and annual and sick leave.
Deadlines: Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program: applications are open through November 6, 2026. Prevention Effectiveness Fellowship: open through January 8, 2027. Evaluation Fellowship Program: opens October 26, 2026 and closes January 7, 2027. Application components vary by fellowship; see CDC's Public Health Fellowships website for details.

item.company: U.S. Department of Transportation (Office of the Secretary)
item.title: 1DOT Internship Program (Pathways)
item.description:
The U.S. Department of Transportation's 1DOT Pathways Internship Program lets aspiring public servants work directly on the operational and policy challenges shaping modern government. Interns are placed across DOT, where they work with engineers, analysts, economists, financial experts, human resources specialists and other professionals to advance national transportation initiatives. The program is expected to begin May 30, 2027, and the temporary appointment is not to exceed September 19, 2027, with a possible extension through the academic year if the intern remains eligible. The program integrates on-the-job training with education at an accredited institution.
Key responsibilities depend on the assigned office and may include: engineering, mathematics, IT, analytical and administrative assignments that build skills and practical experience; assignments that orient and train students in engineering, IT, mathematics, business, economics, management analysis, financial management, safety oversight, human resources, administrative support or transportation program operations; assisting professionals, analysts and program staff with planning, design, maintenance, operation, review and interpretation of business, engineering, mathematics or IT projects related to transportation; and helping develop briefings, reports, presentations, policy documents, communications products, conference materials and executive summaries for leadership. Occupational series include economics, financial management, safety inspection, transportation, information technology, human resources, administrative support, business and industry, community planning, environmental protection, engineering, and mathematics and statistics.
Qualifications: U.S. citizenship is required, and applicants must be at least 16. Students must be enrolled or accepted for enrollment at least half-time at an accredited college, trade school or other qualifying program for Fall 2027, and must keep a 2.5 cumulative GPA. Education levels by grade: GS-03, one academic year of post-high school study; GS-04, two years or an associate's degree; GS-05, four years leading to a bachelor's degree; GS-07, one year of graduate study or superior academic achievement. Students graduating before May 31, 2027 are not eligible unless accepted into an additional qualifying program. Transcripts are required with the application. Preferred fields include engineering, mathematics/statistics, IT, economics, business, public administration, finance, accounting, human resources, communications, management, data analytics and transportation.
Compensation and logistics: Salary is $32,435 to $77,306 per year (GS 3-7). The role is part-time or full-time, with at least 40 hours per week expected in the summer and a flexible part-time schedule during the school year. Interns report to an on-site location, and situational telework may be available. Vacancies are open in 32 locations: Little Rock, AR; Los Angeles, CA; Lakewood, CO; Hartford, CT; Washington, DC; Tallahassee, FL; Atlanta, GA; Ames, IA; Chicago and Matteson, IL; Lake Charles, LA; Cambridge, MA; Lansing, MI; Tupelo, MS; Trenton, NJ; Massena and New York, NY; Columbus, OH; Oklahoma City, OK; Salem, OR; Harrisburg, PA; San Juan, PR; Columbia, SC; Sevierville, TN; Austin, Dallas and Fort Worth, TX; Salt Lake City, UT; Ashburn and McLean, VA; Vancouver, WA; and Madison, WI. Applications are open October 21 to November 3, 2026, and must be submitted by 11:59 PM Eastern on the closing date. Interns may be converted non-competitively to a permanent position, up to GS-12, after meeting all Pathways requirements.

Explore career fields in the acquisition workforce, including engineering, contracting, logistics, business (financial management and cost estimating), information technology, test and evaluation, industrial contract property management, purchasing, science and technology, production, quality and manufacturing, facilities engineering, and program management.
Qualifications: U.S. citizenship is required. Transcripts (official or unofficial) must be submitted with the application, along with proof of full-time enrollment. Students graduating before May 31, 2027 are not eligible unless accepted into an additional qualifying degree program.

Positions are in several locations: Redstone Arsenal, AL; Los Angeles County, CA; Colorado Springs, CO; Patrick AFB, FL; Wright-Patterson AFB, OH; Arlington, VA; and Fort Belvoir, VA. Applications are open October 1 to November 2, 2026, and close at 11:59 PM Eastern on the closing date, or earlier if 500 applications are received. Assist division members with a variety of special projects. Perform routine office and technical work that supports the administration or operation of the division's programs. Use Microsoft Access databases and Excel spreadsheets for data entry, editing, report creation, and monitoring and tracking of activities and efforts.

item.title: Student Trainee (Administration and Office Support)
item.description:
The Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), part of the U.S. Department of the Interior, is hiring Pathways interns, also called Student Trainees, who fill a wide variety of roles and functions in the offices and programs to which they are assigned. This is an open continuous announcement: applications are accepted and reviewed every two weeks until the posted closing date of January 29, 2027 (the announcement opened July 31, 2026). Applicants must be prepared to obtain and maintain Department of State medical, security and suitability clearances. For the 2027 cycle only, conditional offers will be made pending successful completion of the Foreign Service Officer Test (FSOT) and the written exercise of the Foreign Service Officer Assessment (FSOA).
Estimated 2027 timeline (from the posting): FSOT registration runs September 10 to October 30, 2026 and December 31, 2026 to February 5, 2027. The FSOT testing windows are October 10 to 31, 2026 and January 30 to February 6, 2027, and applicants must take the FSOT in one of those windows to meet the application deadline. The application period is December 2026 to January 2027. Candidates are notified in March 2027, finalist interviews are held in Washington, DC in March 2027, offers go out in April 2027, orientation is in June 2027, and the two-year graduate program begins in fall 2027. item.description:

Interns work in a research group led by a Principal Investigator (PI) at one of the NIH Institutes and Centers. Applicants must be 18 by September 30, 2027 (graduating high school seniors who turn 18 by then may qualify if they live within 40 miles of an NIH campus). Applicants must be enrolled at least half-time in an accredited community college, college, university, graduate or professional program at the time of application, or be accepted into an accredited graduate program for the fall. Students interested in biology, engineering, epidemiology, psychology, mathematics, chemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, nursing, physics, computer science, bioinformatics and other health-related fields are invited to apply. Applicants with a family member working at NIH should note the strict nepotism policy, which may limit placement options.
Compensation and logistics: The internship must be completed between May 10 and August 31, 2027, with start and end dates set in consultation with the selecting PI. It is a full-time, in-person commitment; remote and virtual internships are not permitted, and interns must be available for the entire period, with no vacations or summer classes. Stipends are set annually by educational level; the posting does not give amounts. Free parking is available on each campus, NIH does not provide housing, and interns must show proof of health insurance.
How to apply: Apply through the NIH Application Center with a coursework list, CV or resume, a personal statement, and two references. The application closes Tuesday, January 26, 2027 at 12 pm ET, and reference letters are due Tuesday, February 2, 2027 at 12 pm ET. There is no centralized selection: individual PIs review applications and choose their own interns, so applicants should also contact PIs directly. Selection is completed by April 1. ACMER strongly encourages applications from people of Middle Eastern and North African (MENA) descent and from anyone with a demonstrated interest in MENA-related foreign policy, human rights and national security. The program welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.
Program objectives: Promote MENA-American representation in legislative and advocacy processes and encourage engagement with MENA-related issues. Provide substantive, hands-on experience in congressional offices. Strengthen leadership skills and professional networks through structured programming and networking events.
Eligibility: U.S. citizenship is required. Candidates should ideally be pursuing degrees in international affairs, political science, law or a related field, with a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Preference may be given to applicants who live in or attend school within the districts of participating congressional offices.
Program details: The program runs May to August 2027, with exact dates flexible, and full-time schedules are prioritized. The stipend is $5,000 paid by ACMER Foundation, and need-based additional financial assistance may be available. The program is in Washington, DC, interns arrange their own housing and must live in DC for the whole program, and virtual options are not available.
How to apply: Submit four short-answer questions, a PDF resume of two pages at most, a list of two to three references and an unofficial transcript through the application form. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with a priority deadline of December 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT, and the application stays open after that date. Apply only through the application form, not LinkedIn or other job sites. An information session is on November 17 from 5 to 6 PM ET on Zoom. Interviews begin in December, host placement interviews continue through the fall, and a virtual orientation is held in the spring.

item.title: Halle Foundation/AGI Internship (Spring 2027)
item.description:
The Halle Foundation/AGI Internship Program offers paid internships to undergraduate and graduate students at the American-German Institute (AGI), a Washington, DC think tank focused exclusively on the issues at stake for Germany and the United States. Interns get a professional and educational experience at a nonprofit public policy institute that works to build a stronger German-American partnership, and they work within AGI's three program areas: Geoeconomics, Foreign and Security Policy, and Society, Culture and Politics.
Key responsibilities: Research transatlantic issues and, with a senior staff mentor, write an article for the AGI website. Conduct research for fellows and staff. Compile weekly briefs on transatlantic media, defense and immigration. Help with the Institute's social media and marketing strategy. Identify potential partnerships with private firms and grant-giving organizations. Provide logistical and programmatic support for meetings, events and the annual gala, which presents the Global Leadership Award. Interns are evaluated at the mid-point and the end of the internship.
Qualifications: Undergraduate or graduate students interested in transatlantic relations and Europe or Germany, with the equivalent of four semesters of college coursework by the start date. Strong writing, research, organizational and communication skills, attention to detail, and strong computer skills (Microsoft Office, social media, online research). German is preferred but not required. AGI and the Halle Foundation especially encourage applications from students at Georgia colleges and universities and students with ties to Georgia. Foreign nationals must be authorized to work as an intern in the U.S., and AGI does not provide visa sponsorship.
Schedule and compensation: Interns work 28 hours per week, 9:00 to 5:00 Monday through Thursday with an hour for lunch, for the full semester (at least three months). The cycle with a posted deadline is Spring 2027, January to May, with a deadline of November 1, 2026. The cost-of-living stipend is $1,850 per month. Interns arrange their own housing in Washington, DC.
How to apply: AGI does not accept applications through Handshake. Email a single combined PDF with a resume, cover letter, two English writing samples of no more than four pages each, and one letter of recommendation to John Weiller, Operations Coordinator, at jweiller@aicgs.org. The recommender may send the letter confidentially instead.

item.title: ONDCP Unpaid Student Internship (Spring 2027)
item.description:
The Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP), part of the Executive Office of the President, leads and coordinates the nation's drug policy so that it improves the health and lives of the American people. ONDCP develops and implements the National Drug Control Strategy and Budget. This is an unpaid internship in Washington, DC for the Spring 2027 term, which runs from January 19 to May 21, 2027.
Offices accepting interns: Applicants choose one office. The Office of the Director oversees policy development, implementation and coordination. The Office of Addiction Prevention supports federal policy on drug use prevention, early intervention, treatment and recovery. The Office of Grants and Programs manages ONDCP programs, including the High-Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas and Drug-Free Communities programs. The Office of External and Legislative Affairs handles relations with the media, Congress, state, local and Tribal governments and the public. The Office of Management and Administration handles human resources, facilities, procurement, security, IT and the internal budget. The Office of Performance and Budget coordinates budget requests and produces the National Drug Control Assessment. The Office of Supply Elimination develops international supply reduction efforts and coordinates interdiction. The Office of General Counsel provides legal services. The Office of Data and Research coordinates data and research that inform policy.

Availability all day on Tuesday, January 19, 2027 for onboarding, and for the entire session, January 19 through May 21, 2027. Current enrollment, or enrollment to start a program within 5 months of graduation, at least half-time in an accredited undergraduate or graduate college, community college or university. Interns must pass pre-employment security processing and drug testing.
Schedule: Schedules are flexible Monday through Friday, but interns may work only between 7:00 AM and 6:30 PM ET.
How to apply: Email Ramon.d.hamilton@ondcp.eop.gov and Sebastian.a.parker-vaughan@ondcp.eop.gov with a current resume and a one-page cover letter explaining how you could contribute to ONDCP's mission, and name the one office you are applying to. Ignore the default Handshake application window. Applications are due by email no later than 11:59 PM ET on December 4, 2026, and are accepted on a rolling basis. Later applications may be considered for the Summer 2027 session instead.

item.title: Science Policy Fellowship Program (STPI)
item.description:
The Science and Technology Policy Institute (STPI) is a congressionally chartered Federally Funded Research and Development Center operated by the Institute for Defense Analyses (IDA). STPI provides independent analytical support to the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, the National Science Foundation, the National Institutes of Health and other federal agencies on science and technology (S&T) policy. The two-year STPI Science Policy Fellowship Program gives recent bachelor's or master's degree recipients the chance to work on S&T policy areas including space sciences, innovation and competitiveness, energy, health and life sciences, national security, biotechnology, information technologies and STEM education.
Responsibilities: Fellows work with teams of researchers on S&T policy tasks, which may include survey and interview research, database development, data visualization, statistical techniques and other qualitative and quantitative methods for project-driven policy analysis. Over two years, fellows take part in analyses that support federal policymakers, interact with White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and other federal science agency staff, join workshops and discussions, receive mentorship from STPI research staff, train on analytical methods and tools, and attend and present at select professional society meetings.
Qualifications: This is a full-time position open only to recent bachelor's or master's degree recipients; candidates with higher degrees will not be considered. Candidates must have a bachelor's degree conferred between May 2025 and July 2027, or, for master's applicants, a bachelor's conferred between May 2024 and July 2026. Degrees in engineering, life sciences, physical sciences, social and behavioral sciences, computer science, mathematical sciences, statistics and learning sciences are encouraged. A strong interest in S&T policy is expected, though policy experience is not required. Strong written and oral communication skills and the ability to support team efforts. U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and keep a security clearance are required.
Compensation: Annual stipends are $73,000 in year 1 and $74,500 in year 2 for Baccalaureate Fellows, and $81,000 in year 1 and $82,500 in year 2 for Science Policy Fellows. IDA lists benefits including a 10% retirement contribution, 20 days of paid time off, tuition reimbursement and eligibility for Public Service Loan Forgiveness.
How to apply: Apply through the link on IDA's careers page, then email a personal statement of 500 words or fewer, a writing sample of up to 2,500 words (sole author), and unofficial transcripts to STPI-Fellow@ida.org. Finalists are asked to arrange two academic recommendation letters sent directly to that address. All materials are due by January 4, 2027.
